title: Rust: Sorting Algorithms
description: Implement sorting algorithms and use Rust's built-in sort methods.

steps.title: Built-in sort
steps.description: Sort the array `[5, 2, 8, 1, 9]` using `.sort()` and print the result.

steps.title: Bubble Sort
steps.description: Implement bubble sort manually. Write a function `bubble_sort(arr: &mut [i32])` that sorts in place. Test with `[4, 3, 2, 1]`.
hints: Loop through the array, swapping adjacent elements if out of order.
Repeat until no swaps are needed.
Bubble sort has O(n²) time complexity.

steps.title: Quicksort
steps.description: Implement quicksort: `fn quicksort(arr: &mut [i32])`. Pick a pivot, partition, and recursively sort. Test with `[7, 2, 9, 1, 5]`.
hints: Choose the last element as pivot.
Partition: move smaller elements left, larger right.
Recursively sort the left and right partitions.

verification.failureMessage: Quicksort [7,2,9,1,5] and print the sorted result.

steps.title: Custom Sort with Comparator
steps.description: Use `.sort_by()` with a custom comparator to sort strings `["apple", "banana", "kiwi", "strawberry"]` by length (shortest first).
hints: Shortest first: kiwi, apple, banana, strawberry

verification.failureMessage: Sort strings by length and print.

steps.title: Stable Sort
steps.description: Given `[(3, "a"), (1, "b"), (2, "c"), (1, "d")]`, sort by the first element using `.sort_by_key()` (which is stable) and verify equal keys maintain original relative order.
hints: `pairs.sort_by_key(|p| p.0);` — stable sort by first element.
Print sorted pairs to verify order.

verification.successMessage: Stable sort preserves original order of equal keys!
verification.failureMessage: Sort pairs and print — (1,b) should come before (1,d).
